title: Evaporation cools a surface because breaking water's bonds takes heat
summary: Evaporation cools the surroundings, because heat is spent breaking the bonds between water molecules.
body: The U.S. Geological Survey says that because energy is required to break the bonds holding water molecules together, evaporation removes heat from the environment and leads to a net cooling. The page's picture is an alcohol pad on an arm before an injection: the alcohol evaporates quickly and the skin feels cold, because some heat leaves with it. The example is alcohol, used to show the same bond-breaking idea the page has just stated for water. It is not a medical instruction.
